With charities under strain — from economic pressure, changes to federal programs and a suspended Combined Federal Campaign — Laredo's nonprofits are putting out a direct call for volunteers and donations, according to a Cuidando Lo Nuestro column by the United Way of Laredo in the Laredo Morning Times.

The most urgent date: October 31 is the last day for Texas state employees to make online payroll deductions through the Texas State Employee Charitable Campaign, a program created by legislation in 1993, at secctexasgiving.org. The column names Bethany House, the Salvation Army, Catholic Charities, the Webb County Community Action Agency and the Kidney Foundation among the providers helping with meals, housing, rent, utilities, mortgage assistance, dialysis transportation and shelter services.

The volunteer needs are specific. The Salvation Army is taking applications for Bell Ringers. United Way's Laredo Volunteers for Literacy needs tutors for English as a Second Language, citizenship, computer and digital literacy, and financial literacy — 47 students were waiting for tutors, with more information at unitedwaylaredo.org. Volunteer Income Tax Assistance needs tax-preparation volunteers, with certification training beginning soon through Catholic Charities, United Way or VITA. The South Texas Food Bank and Laredo Regional Food Bank need groups to assemble distribution bags for seniors and families, and the Laredo Animal Protective Society and Best Friends for Life need fosters, dog walkers, cat groomers and feeders.

Donations of goods matter too: Goodwill and the Salvation Army accept thrift-store items, while Casa de Misericordia and Bethany House help clients moving from shelter to housing and need furniture, pots and pans, and towels; Bethany House's Mission give was seeking blankets, jackets, socks and other new or gently used items.

Two dates to put on the calendar: the United Way Volunteers for Literacy Adult Spelling Bee on November 5 at the Falcon Bank Event Center, and Keep Laredo Beautiful's Arbor Day tree planting on November 7 at Divine Mercy Park, with a goal of 200 trees.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, “Cuidando Lo Nuestro: Volunteer opportunities help local charities,” October 25, 2026.

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: With an October 31 deadline for state employees' charitable payroll deductions, Laredo nonprofits are calling for volunteers — 47 literacy students are waiting for tutors — plus donations of household goods for families moving out of shelters.
title: Cuidando Lo Nuestro: Laredo charities call for volunteers and donations as October 31 giving deadline nears
